claims.text: The lower-adjoined family \(\{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}\) minimally generates \(J_v\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 220-235]

**Indecomposable-basis lemma.** Let \(A=\bigoplus_{d\ge0}A_d\) be a graded \(\mathbb Z\)-algebra with \(A_0=\mathbb Z\), let \(J\) be a graded ideal, and let \(G\subset J\) be a finite homogeneous generating set. If the images of \(G\) in \(J/A_+J\) are \(\mathbb Z\)-linearly independent, then they are a homogeneous \(\mathbb Z\)-basis of \(J/A_+J\). Hence \(J/A_+J\) is torsion-free and its Hilbert series is \(\sum_{g\in G}z^{\deg g}\).
Minimality does not imply the independence hypothesis: for \(A=\mathbb Z[x]\), \(J=(2x,x^2)\), and \(G=\{2x,x^2\}\), \(G\) is irredundant but \(J/xJ\cong\mathbb Z\oplus\mathbb Z/2\).
